newsitem.title: USA: NYS makes little headway with GAAP deficit - Moody's.
newsitem.headline: NYS makes little headway with GAAP deficit - Moody's.

text.p: Due to a pension financing, New York State would only slightly cut a big deficit measured under Generally Accepted Accounted Principles (GAAP) under a proposed budget, Moody's Investors Service said Tuesday.

Bob Kurtter, a Moody's analyst, explained that the fiscal 1997 cash surplus would help produce a GAAP operating surplus though drawing that down in fiscal 1998 produces an operating deficit, under Gov George Pataki's proposed plan. "The net effect of the two years is that the GAAP deficit is expected to be reduced slightly," Kurtter said, in prepared remarks.

But the analyst noted the drop is achieved with a Taxable Pension Obligation financing that was done through the Dormitory Authority in 1996. This produced a $300 million positive impact on the GAAP balance.
